jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor of School Psychology
jobs.institution: University of Washington: College of Education
jobs.description:
The College of Education at the University of Washington invites applications for a teaching faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor with an anticipated start date of September 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in teaching and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. The successful candidate will join our faculty on a full-time basis for a nine-month academic appointment with a 3-year term beginning September 16, 2027. Renewal of the appointment will be considered in the second year.
The base salary range for this position will be $8,466 - $9,046/per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination. Other compensation associated with this position may include a limited commitment of summer salary based on curricular need and available funding.
The successful candidate will be expected to:
Teach full-time in the School Psychology Program (7-9 courses across 3 quarters per academic year)
Advise specialist-level graduate students in the School Psychology Program
Educate and supervise school psychology students who practice in schools and as health service providers
Engage in scholarly work that is culturally responsive with a particular focus on youth, families, and communities
Demonstrate scholarship by introducing new knowledge or methods into course content; creating or using innovative pedagogical methods; collaborating on new courses, curricula, or course materials; and/or seeking external funds to support innovations or students
Contribute to the operation and development of the School Psychology Program
Work collaboratively with faculty in the College Area, which includes programs in Special Education, Applied Behavior Analysis, and Measurement and Statistics
Engage in faculty governance
Engage in service, commensurate with rank, at the College, University, local, state, or national level that advances the teaching mission of the university
The nationally ranked UW College of Education dedicates its resources to making excellent education a daily reality for all students and is committed to solving real-world educational challenges and closing opportunity gaps. Members of the College maintain a set of active partnerships with more than 300 educational institutions in the region, state, and nation—schools, school districts, community-based organizations, informal educational institutions, and professional organizations. Our College’s mission leads us to invest in recruiting colleagues who demonstrate experience with, knowledge of, and a commitment to working with culturally diverse communities to address pressing educational challenges and foster a more just and caring society. University of Washington faculty engage in teaching, research, and service.
Please visit us on the web to learn more about the University of Washington (http://www.washington.edu) and the College of Education (https://education.uw.edu/), and our mission and goals, research and outreach activities, faculty, and academic programs.

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Scholar - Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CD)
jobs.institution: Case Western Reserve University: Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering (PD)
jobs.description:
The Duval Lab in the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering invites applications for a postdoctoral researcher to conduct research in the field of separation science and technology. Our research group has developed unique expertise in the design, prototyping, and implementation of rotating packed bed contactors for resource recovery and water treatment. This technology fits in the broader scope of our laboratory research which focuses on developing new materials and processes for critical metals and elements. The postdoctoral researcher will work collaboratively with our university-, national laboratory- and industry-partners to design ion-exchange and adsorption separation processes using this prototyped equipment.
This research will occur in the brand-new Roger E. Suzi Interdisciplinary Research Building on Case Western Reserve University’s campus as part of the Advanced Materials and Manufacturing cluster.
Responsibilities and Duties:
Experimental work will include synthesizing and testing adsorptive resins for metals separations, measuring resin uptake and selectivity using batch and on-column measurements (commercial and synthesized in lab), modifying prototype designs to meet process needs, selecting appropriate solution-phase and resin chemistries to improve the separation metrics of throughput, productivity, selectivity, and/or product capture.
This postdoctoral researcher will join a sub-group in our lab dedicated to this class of process equipment forming a community of practice. The individual is expected to complete technical milestones, participate in weekly meetings with collaborators, contribute to regular project reporting, attend annual review meetings, and lead the characterization efforts at CWRU. The postdoctoral scholar will report directly to PI Christine Duval.
In compliance with the City of Cleveland’s Pay Transparency Ordinance (effective October 27, 2025), the annual starting base salary range for this position is $55,000 -$62,652. CWRU considers factors such as (but not limited to) the specific grant funding and the terms of the research grant when extending an offer. Postdocs receive individual and family healthcare benefits, life insurance, and employee assistance.

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor of Musicology
jobs.description:
The Carnegie Mellon University School of Music invites applications for our Assistant Teaching Professor of Musicology position. College- or university-level teaching experience, including undergraduate music history survey courses for music majors, is strongly preferred. Applicants should be engaged with contemporary musicological research, issues, and teaching methods. We seek applicants who will work with existing faculty to sustain and grow the music history core curriculum and develop compelling and relevant electives. Founded in 1912, CMU's School of Music offers Bachelor of Fine Arts and Master of Music degrees in instrumental, piano, and vocal performance and composition; a Bachelor of Fine Arts in electronic music; and a Master of Music in collaborative piano. In collaboration with the School of Computer Science and the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, the School also offers both a Bachelor of Science and a Master of Science in Music and Technology. With 42 full-time faculty, 55 part-time faculty (including 22 from the Grammy-Award-winning Pittsburgh Symphony), and 13 administrative and technical staff, Carnegie Mellon's School of Music blends the one-on-one conservatory model of musical mentorship with the resources and research capacities of an R1 university. jobs.title: Emergency Medicine Physician,  Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor, Emergency Medicine, EH Site Director
jobs.description:
The Department of Emergency Medicine at Stony Brook University Hospital and the Renaissance School of Medicine at Stony Brook University are seeking a motivated, organized, and collaborative physician to serve as Medical Director of the East Hampton Emergency Department.
The Medical Director will provide physician leadership and administrative oversight for the East Hampton Emergency Department while working closely with departmental and health-system leadership to maintain the delivery of high-quality, patient-centered emergency care. The Medical Director will serve as the physician leader and face of the East Hampton Emergency Department, representing the site within Stony Brook Medicine and fostering strong relationships with physicians, staff, patients, the surrounding community, and health-system leadership.
The successful candidate will be a motivated and highly organized physician with demonstrated leadership ability and a strong commitment to clinical excellence, teamwork, patient safety, quality improvement, and medical education. The ideal candidate will possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills, an enthusiasm for working with and educating emergency medicine residents, and an interest in contributing to the continued development of emergency medical services at the East Hampton site.
The successful candidate should embrace the opportunity to be the visible physician leader and face of the East Hampton Emergency Department, establishing a consistent leadership presence and serving as an advocate for the site’s physicians, staff, patients, and educational mission within the larger Stony Brook Medicine system.
Responsibilities
The Medical Director will be responsible for the clinical, educational, and administrative leadership of the site, with responsibilities including:
Ensuring appropriate and reliable physician coverage and assisting with the development and maintenance of the physician schedule. The candidate will be the point person for all issues relating to the East Hampton Emergency Department.
Serving as the visible physician leader and representative of the East Hampton Emergency Department, promoting the mission and values of Stony Brook Medicine and fostering a culture of clinical excellence, professionalism, collaboration, and engagement among the entire Emergency Department team.
Promoting adherence to departmental, hospital, and health-system policies, procedures, and clinical standards.
Supporting and advancing quality improvement and patient-safety initiatives within the Emergency Department.
Participating in the review of clinical cases, quality metrics, patient-care concerns, and opportunities for improvement.
Conducting regular staff meetings, including monthly meetings as appropriate, to facilitate communication, address operational concerns, and advance departmental goals.
Providing educational support and clinical guidance to physicians, advanced practice providers, nursing staff, and other members of the Emergency Department team as appropriate.
Supporting the educational mission of the Department of Emergency Medicine through the active presence and participation of emergency medicine residents at the East Hampton site. The Medical Director will help foster a welcoming and academically engaging clinical environment, encourage meaningful resident involvement in patient care, and support bedside teaching, mentorship, and educational opportunities that enhance the residents’ clinical experience.
Working collaboratively with residency and departmental educational leadership to ensure that the East Hampton experience contributes meaningfully to resident education while maintaining the highest standards of patient care and supervision.
Working collaboratively with nursing leadership, hospital administration, and Department of Emergency Medicine leadership to identify and address clinical and operational needs.
Supporting a culture of professionalism, collegiality, accountability, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Serving as a physician liaison between the East Hampton Emergency Department and the broader Stony Brook Medicine emergency medicine system.
Compensation:
Qualified candidates can expect a competitive physician salary with an additional Site Medical Director stipend commensurate with the responsibilities of the position.
This position represents an opportunity to assume a meaningful leadership role within the Department of Emergency Medicine at Stony Brook University Hospital and the Renaissance School of Medicine while helping to shape and support the delivery of outstanding emergency care to the East Hampton community and contributing to the education and professional development of the next generation of emergency physicians.

jobs.title: 2027-28 Visiting Assistant Professor (VAP) in the Management Communication Program
jobs.institution: New York University: Management Communication Program
jobs.description:
The Management Communication Program at the Stern School of Business is accepting applications for a Visiting Assistant Professor (VAP). This position is designed for recent (within 4 years) PhD recipients.
The VAP will teach 4 sections in the first-year, writing-intensive courses required in Stern's undergraduate program: Commerce & Culture (fall) and Business & Society (spring). This writing-intensive curriculum examines the relationship between business and society to build students’ writing and critical-thinking skills while introducing them to business inquiry. The fall course, Commerce & Culture, focuses on representations of business in fiction—novels, films, plays, and short stories. Through discussion-based sessions and analytical papers, students examine how texts portray the interplay of market forces, society, and individuals. The spring course, Business & Society, turns to the theoretical texts underlying economic and business discourse (from Adam Smith to Elinor Ostrom to R. Edward Freeman), teaching students to engage with conceptual texts and apply them to contemporary business situations. Writing assignments include analytical claims about conceptual ideas, research-based analysis of social issues, and proposals for business action.
In addition to teaching these small, interdisciplinary seminar classes, VAPs will work closely with an assigned faculty mentor, coordinate with course directors about texts or concepts from their area of expertise that may add to the curriculum, and have the opportunity to take on additional roles such as supervising the courses' undergraduate teaching fellows or developing instructional programming.
Appointments are for an initial term of two years, and may be renewed for up to one additional year, for a maximum appointment period of three years, contingent upon satisfactory performance reviews, program teaching needs, and mutual agreement. VAPs are non-tenure track.
In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $60,000 - $80,000. This pay range represents base pay only (for 9 months) and excludes any additional items such as incentives, bonuses, clinical compensation, or other items. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer.

jobs.title: Director, Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: School of Medicine
jobs.description:
The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine seeks a visionary physician leader, scholar, and steward of academic medicine to serve as the next Director of the Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery. This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a department with a distinctive legacy in complex reconstruction and to advance its missions in education, research, and clinical care.
Johns Hopkins School of Medicine is a global leader in biomedical discovery, medical education, and patient care, supported by a collaborative academic and clinical environment and a longstanding commitment to excellence, integrity, and service. The Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery contributes to this mission through outstanding clinical care and training, advancing work across all three pillars of university’s mission.
The department has helped define the frontiers of reconstructive transplantation – highlighted by landmark bilateral arm transplants – and maintains internationally recognized leadership in peripheral nerve surgery, targeted muscle reinnervation, and complex microvascular reconstruction. These distinctive capabilities uniquely position the department to shape the future of care of patients with complex, life-altering conditions.
The next Director will build on these distinctive strengths and guide the department’s continued growth as the need for complex care increases and the field evolves. The successful candidate will provide strategic vision, foster respectful collaboration and inclusion, and advance the department’s work across all mission areas. Opportunities in evolving areas of the field, including nerve surgery and transplantation, underscore the potential for continued growth and impact.
Serving as the face of the department and a representative of Johns Hopkins locally, nationally, and globally, the Director must embody honesty and integrity, effective communication, collaborative leadership, and sound judgment. The ideal candidate will excel at the highest level while recognizing and supporting the importance of each part of the university’s mission.
The Director will provide overall stewardship of the department, including strategic planning, fiscal oversight, faculty and trainee development, and the advancement of clinical care, education, and research. The successful candidate will demonstrate financial acumen, executive leadership experience, and a commitment to inclusivity. The Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory (LDEO) of Columbia University invites applications for the Lamont-Brinson Postdoctoral Fellowship in earthquake physics, fault structure and mechanics, and related fields. We seek candidates whose research uses field or laboratory experiments or observation-driven computational methods in seismology, geodesy, or geology. Candidates who use AI/ML approaches are especially encouraged to apply. The successful candidate is expected to perform research broadly related to LDEO's "Anticipating Earthquakes" Initiative (https://lamont.columbia.edu/anticipating-earthquakes) within the Seimology, Geology, and Tectonophysics Division (SGT). The initiative aims at improving our understanding of the relationship between active faults and the earthquakes they generate.
Columbia University policy allows for postdoctoral researchers to complete up to five years of service in a postdoctoral role across all institutions. As this position is a fixed-term of two years with an anticipated start date of June 1, 2027, the chosen candidate should be eligible to complete two years of service in this role and should not have more than three years of experience in a postdoctoral role at any institution by June 1, 2027. Candidate would be ineligible to complete two years of service in a postdoctoral role at Columbia will not be considered.
The principal selection criteria for Lamont-Brinson Postdoctoral Fellows are scientific excellent and a clearly expressed proposal to perform research under the mentorship of one or more faculty within LDEO's SGT division (https://lamont.columbia.edu/research-divisions/seismology-geology-tectonophysics). Candidates that work on interests of multiple research or instructional faculty are preferred. and are encouraged to contact potential mentors. The deadline for applications for the Lamont-Brinson Postdoctoral Fellowship is December 31, 2026. Lamont-Brinson Postdoctoral Fellowships are supported for 12 months per year, include a $7,500 research allowance, and carry an annual salary of $72,116.

jobs.title: Implementation Science in Neuroscience — Open Rank Academic Investigator (Tenure-eligible)
jobs.institution: University of Virginia: Public Health Sciences
jobs.description:
The University of Virginia (UVA) Department of Public Health Sciences (PHS), in partnership with the UVA Brain Institute, is seeking applicants for an open-rank, tenure-track/tenure-eligible faculty position within the Division of Health Intervention & Implementation Science. This position channels an existing UVA Grand Challenges investment in neuroscience toward a defined implementation science charge, and the candidate will develop and lead a multidisciplinary research program, along with contributing to team science collaboration, in support of the department's and the Brain Institute's mission.
UVA has committed a Grand Challenges research investment of more than $75M to the Brain Institute — the University's largest-ever investment in neuroscience — supporting bold, collaborative work spanning Alzheimer's disease, autism, epilepsy, and brain function and development across the lifespan. This position ties directly into that investment, applying an implementation science lens to help ensure the resulting discoveries reach patients, providers, and communities. The successful candidate will preferably focus their research on the implementation and dissemination of evidence-based practices in one or more areas of brain health, such as neurodegenerative disease, stroke and cerebrovascular recovery, psychiatric and mood disorders, mental health, substance use, or neurodevelopmental conditions, though deep neuroscience content expertise is not a prerequisite. With numerous active and planned statewide initiatives in rural health and collaborations with the UVA Karen S. Rheuban Center for Telehealth, the successful candidate will have ample opportunity to advance innovation in health care in Virginia.
This role is one of several coordinated positions PHS is recruiting as part of a broader departmental commitment to implementation science, anchored by the UVA IMPACT Hub (Implementation Methods, Partnerships, and Community Translation). The successful candidate will be an active member of the Hub, joining a cross-Grounds peer community of implementation scientists whose applied work spans cancer, education and human development, and clinical care. The successful applicant must be motivated, independent, and highly organized, with excellent written and verbal communication skills. Finally, the successful applicant will have teaching and service responsibilities and is expected to participate in appropriate national and international organizations.
Faculty in this position will be active participants in the UVA Brain Institute, the University's hub for interdisciplinary neuroscience research connecting faculty, students, and staff across Grounds, and will also be affiliated with the UVA IMPACT Hub, which provides methodological consultation and a peer community of implementation scientists working across the University, and which connects to UVA's broader clinical and translational science infrastructure, including its reimagined Clinical and Translational Science Award (CTSA) effort. PHS offers a vibrant academic home with access to support services for research. The department provides comprehensive and multi-disciplinary scientific and analytical services to the University of Virginia School of Medicine through its Divisions of Biostatistics & Health Data Science; Health Evaluation & Outcomes Science; and Health Intervention & Implementation Science. The Department offers two master's degrees, an MS in Clinical Research and an MPH, a Certificate in Public Health, and is planning a Certificate in Implementation Science. Successful candidates will contribute to the design and implementation of the graduate education curriculum; teach intermediate and advanced graduate-level methods courses; conduct research; and advance scholarship in their area of expertise. More information about PHS is available at https://med.virginia.edu/phs.

jobs.title: Director of Operations, Communications and Marketing
jobs.description:
The Director of Operations is a member of the Communications and Marketing division's leadership team. The director is responsible for the systems, processes, and planning that connect the division's strategic and creative work. The director assesses how work moves through the division today, then builds or rebuilds the intake, project management, and reporting systems that keep the division responsive, organized, and focused on institutional priorities. Working closely with the Vice President, the director leads production planning, anticipates upcoming needs, and ensures that work reflects the College's standards for quality. The director also represents the division to campus partners and serves as a key operational leader as the division evolves.

Leadership
• Serve as a member of the division's leadership team, contributing to planning, priorities, and decision-making
• Represent the Vice President in meetings with campus offices as delegated
• Partner with the Vice President on division-wide initiatives and organizational development
Intake and workflow
• Assess the division's current intake process and build on or redesign it, including scoping conversations with campus partners before work begins
• Set and communicate realistic timelines, formats, and deliverables for each request
• Prioritize and route work to the strategic and creative teams, including web and digital, based on institutional priorities and team capacity
• Close the loop with requesters and ensure a consistent, high-quality experience for campus partners
Project management and production
• Assess the division's project management systems, currently Smartsheet, and build on or redesign them to support consistent use across teams
• Lead regular production meetings to track active work, resolve bottlenecks, and anticipate upcoming needs
• Build and maintain the division's editorial and production calendars in coordination with strategic and creative leads
• Flag risks early and keep projects on schedule from start to finish
Crisis and rapid response operations
• Support the Executive Director for Strategic Communications in crisis and rapid response situations by managing workflow, approvals, timelines, and distribution
• Maintain the division's crisis protocols, contact lists, approval chains, and message distribution procedures, and help coordinate response logistics across the division
Standards and quality
• Understand and uphold the division's brand, editorial, and creative standards throughout the production process
• Work with the Creative Director, the Director of Web and Digital Experience, and strategic leads to ensure work meets expectations for quality before it is delivered
Budget and vendor management
• Manage the division's operating budget, including forecasting, tracking, and reporting
• Administer agency and vendor contracts, statements of work, and invoicing, in partnership with the division leaders who direct each vendor's work
• Ensure vendor work is coordinated with in-house teams and delivered on scope and on budget
Reporting and measurement
• Develop regular reporting on workload, turnaround times, project outcomes, and budget to inform staffing and investment decisions
• Identify process improvements and document standards and workflows for the division
Partnership and service
• Serve as the primary operational point of contact for campus partners on project requests
• Build strong working relationships with offices across the College, including Advancement, Enrollment Management, and Athletics
Future team development

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor, Clinical Biostatistics
jobs.institution: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center: Clinical Research Division
jobs.description:
Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center seeks a faculty member at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level to join the Clinical Biostatistics Program within the Clinical Research Division (CRD).
The Clinical Biostatistics Program currently consists of 6 faculty and 11 statistical research associates (SRAs). It is a highly collaborative and methodologically diverse unit that serves as an essential statistical and scientific partner to investigators across Fred Hutch, the University of Washington, national cooperative groups, and numerous academic and clinical research institutions. Our work reflects extensive engagement across basic, translational, and clinical research programs.
Collectively, the Clinical Biostatistics Program Faculty and SRAs provide expertise spanning clinical trial design and conduct, survival analysis, competing risks methodology, cancer survivorship, transplantation outcomes research, immunotherapy, biomarker development, precision oncology (including master protocols), pragmatic trial design elements, statistical genetics, bioinformatics, machine learning, and the analysis of high-dimensional molecular data.
Successful candidates are expected to engage in collaborative and independent statistical research. Key areas of research that are particularly desirable for this position are: survival analysis, competing risks methodology, transplantation outcomes, graft versus host disease, immunotherapy, and clinical trial design (early to mid-phase). Other desirable areas of expertise include cancer survivorship, late effects, infectious complications, cumulative burden of morbidity, longitudinal methods, and genomic/proteomic research.
Faculty are expected to perform their primary activities on-site at Fred Hutch.
The rich biostatistics environment at the center includes over 70 PhD-level biostatisticians (member-track faculty and staff scientists) across the Clinical Research, Public Health Sciences, and Vaccine and Infectious Diseases Divisions. Biostatisticians across the center also engage in collaborative and independent statistical research, including efforts with coordinating and statistical and data management centers for the Women’s Health Initiative, the SWOG Cancer Research Network, the Cancer Screening Research Network, the HIV Vaccine Trials Network, and the HIV Prevention Trials Network.
Fred Hutch is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center in Washington.
With a track record of global leadership in bone marrow transplantation, HIV/AIDS prevention, immunotherapy, and COVID-19 vaccines, Fred Hutch has earned a reputation as one of the world’s leading cancer, infectious disease and biomedical research centers. Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures for the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.
At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities makes us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.
